AstraNova Biotech - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AstraNova Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad and wait for further instructions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AstraNova Biotech's financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are David Kwon, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Vargas, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Michael Torres, Chief Scientific Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Kwon, CEO of AstraNova Biotech.

David Kwon, CEO:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. AstraNova Biotech delivered a strong performance in the Q3, driven by robust new product launches and meaningful market share gains across our oncology and immunology portfolios. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, with a particular emphasis on our new product launches and the impressive market share momentum we're seeing. As you know, 2024 has been a pivotal year for AstraNova Biotech, marked by two major launches that are accelerating our shift into high-growth areas like oncology and rare diseases. Let me share the latest insights from IQVIA NPA and Xponent data as of the end of Q3.

Starting with our flagship antibody-drug conjugate, NovaLink™, a trastuzumab deruxtecan analog enhanced by our proprietary linker-payload technology, which earned FDA accelerated approval in February for second-line HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer. Just six months after launch, NovaLink has surpassed our initial forecasts. In Q3, U.S. net sales reached $285 million, reflecting a 45% increase quarter-over-quarter and bringing year-to-date sales to $612 million. On a moving annual total basis through September, we've secured 18% share in the U.S. HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer market—an impressive gain of 8 percentage points since launch. This progress has come primarily from Roche's Kadcyla, where we've captured 4 points of share, and even from AstraZeneca/Daiichi's Enhertu in overlapping patient groups, gaining 2 points.

The momentum stems from strong adoption among peak prescribers—the top 20% of oncologists—who now account for 65% of NovaLink prescriptions, with new-to-brand prescriptions surging 32% quarter-over-quarter to more than 28,000 weekly. Patient compliance remains excellent at 82% refill rates, bolstered by our NovaAssist patient support program, which has reached 72% of eligible patients. On the manufacturing side, we've scaled up at our Singapore ADC facility to 50,000 vials per month, utilizing our click-chemistry linker technology to deliver a 25% higher drug-to-antibody ratio compared to first-generation ADCs, which reduces off-target toxicity as confirmed in our Phase 2 bystander effect data published in Nature Medicine last quarter.

Geographically, the U.S. dominates with 92% of sales, but Europe is gaining traction. Following EMA approval in July, we've recorded €42 million in Q3 sales in Germany, France, and the UK, achieving 12% share in markets traditionally led by Kadcyla, according to IQVIA MIDAS. In China, our partnership with Fosun Pharma has submitted for NMPA approval, targeting a H1 2025 launch; early access programs are already providing 5,000 patient-months of data to support expansion into HER2-low gastric cancer.

Strategically, NovaLink is priced at a 15% premium to Enhertu—$14,200 per vial—backed by superior progression-free survival from our head-to-head emulation analysis, showing 18.2 months versus 16.4 months. Payer acceptance is solid, with 85% gross-to-net adjustments, including top-tier placements at CVS Caremark and Express Scripts. For 2025, we're projecting peak U.S. sales of $1.4 to 1.6 billion, with the Phase 3 readout for frontline metastatic breast cancer in Q4 potentially unlocking an additional 20% of the addressable patient population.

Moving to our second key launch, RheumaBlock™, our oral covalent BTK inhibitor for relapsed/refractory rheumatoid arthritis, approved in May via priority review. It generated $112 million in Q3 U.S. sales and $198 million year-to-date, capturing 14% share in the moderate-to-severe RA biologic-naïve segment per Symphony Health. We've gained 6 points from AbbVie's Rinvoq and J&J's Tremfya, thanks to once-daily dosing and a favorable cardiac safety profile—no QT prolongation in our 2,500-patient database.

Technologically, our AI-optimized covalent warhead cuts off-target kinase inhibition by 40% relative to earlier ibrutinib-based therapies, as showcased at EULAR 2024. U.S. uptake is widespread, with 52% new-to-brand prescription penetration among rheumatologists and total prescriptions up 28% quarter-over-quarter. Europe filings target Q1 2025 approval, while our Japan out-licensing to Eisai has delivered ¥8 billion in upfront payments plus royalties.

In Asia-Pacific, early access in South Korea through Samsung Bioepis has yielded 22% regional share gains, riding the biosimilar erosion against Humira equivalents.

In aggregate, these launches are powering 22% organic revenue growth year-to-date, with gross margins at 78% due to enhanced CMC yields. Broader market dynamics are supportive—global ADC sales are forecasted to reach $30 billion by 2028 according to Evaluate Pharma, and BTK inhibitors are expanding into autoimmunity. While biosimilar pressures on legacy TNF inhibitors are intensifying, our next-generation platforms like PROTACs and bispecifics provide a strong competitive moat.

We're raising our FY2024 guidance for new product sales to $1.0 to 1.1 billion, anticipating 25-30% market share expansion. Now, I'll hand over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, for a detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Chen, CFO:
Thank you, David. As David highlighted, we had a solid Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, an increase of 16% compared to the same period last year. This growth was primarily driven by volume expansion from NovaLink and RheumaBlock launches, partially offset by modest pricing adjustments in mature markets.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $480 million, or $1.28 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $650 million, or $1.73 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.65 billion, reflecting continued investments in R&D to advance our pipeline while maintaining operational efficiencies. Our cash position remains strong at $4.5 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to $11.0 to $11.4 billion in revenue, implying 14-18% growth.

Before diving deeper into forward-looking elements, let me provide a detailed geographic revenue breakdown, emphasizing the robust expansion in emerging markets that supports our diversification strategy beyond mature regions. This aligns with unmet needs in oncology, immunology, and rare diseases that match our innovative lineup.

Total net product revenues reached $2.8 billion, up 16% year-over-year reported and 18% on a constant-currency basis. Excluding a $150 million one-time milestone from our PD-1 collaboration in China, core growth was 13%.

U.S. revenue: $1.71 billion, or 61% of total—up 9% YoY. Led by NovaLink at $850 million (up 45% from launch momentum) and RheumaBlock contributing $420 million (up 28%). Share gains tie to NovaLink's expanded label in key indications. Headwinds from the Inflation Reduction Act increased gross-to-net by 200 basis points, with Medicare Part D rebates at 28%. Still, gross margins held at 82% via efficiencies at our Devens facility. We anticipate mid-single-digit U.S. growth in H2 as biosimilar erosion hits legacy assets.

Europe: $720 million, or 26%—up 13% at constant currency despite 3% FX drag from the euro. Tender wins in Germany and Italy for RheumaBlock secured 65% new script share per IQVIA, and NovaLink launched across EU5, ramping to $130 million. Volume dips in CEE from payer austerity were offset by partnerships like Accord Healthcare. Europe now at 28% of innovative sales.

Rest of World: $370 million, or 13%—up 30% YoY. Emerging markets drove this, at $310 million or 11% total (35% YoY growth). China: $190 million, up 48%, with NovaLink at $115 million post-NMPA inclusion in NRDL; volumes 3x U.S. levels. Our WuXi JV cut lead times 40%. India/SE Asia: $60 million, up 32%, via Cipla partnerships. Latin America: $45 million, up 20%, with Eurofarma tenders. Other EM: $15 million, up 25%, via Saudi SFDA fast-tracks.

This EM surge results from regulatory acceleration (12 filings cut times 18 months), localized pricing (85% adherence via access funds), supply resilience (40% localized production), and tailored trials (30% Phase III sites in EM).

For Q4, EM at $340-360 million (32%+ growth); FY EM ~$1.2 billion, 12% total. Positions us for 16-20% CAGR to 2027.

Shifting to revenue guidance and catalysts: For Q4 2024, raising to $480-505 million, 24-29% growth over Q4 2023, from NovaLink strength and $30 million Takeda milestones. FY2024 now $1.95-2.05 billion, 27% growth midpoint, 85% product sales. 2025 initial: $2.4-2.6 billion, 25-30% growth, with NovaLink follow-ons.

U.S. 22% growth via payer deals; ex-U.S. 38% from reimbursement wins like Germany's AMNOG for NovaLink.

Catalysts: Q4 Phase 3 NovaLink-301 topline in HER2-low BC (HR 0.62 PFS); Feb 2025 PDUFA NovaTarg NSCLC expansion (+14 mo OS, $250M incremental); Q1 2025 NovaGene-101 DMD interim; Q2 NovaSlim-OR obesity data (18% weight loss). R&D flat 28% revenue; $1.2B cash to 2027.

Now, on R&D expense and priorities: Q3 R&D at $920 million, up 20% YoY, 33% of revenue. FY $3.5-3.6 billion, 28% revenues. Trending from 22% in 2021 to focus Phase 2/3; PTRS 25% vs. industry 12-15%.

Breakdown: 45% oncology ($414M), NovaLink-301 Phase 3 ($160M, 1,300 patients); 30% rare diseases ($276M), Nova-GT-102 DMD Phase 2 complete (85% biomarkers); 20% immunology ($184M), Nova-BiS-450 Phase 3 ($130M); 5% platforms ($46M).

U.S. 60%, Europe 25%, APAC 15% (WuXi trials). Diversified modalities; $500M M&A firepower. Q4 $950M; FY25 26% revenue.

Key assumptions: FY2024 $11.2-11.6B revenue midpoint 15% growth; NovaLink $3.0B (30% up). U.S. pricing 92% list; Europe 5% erosion. Pipeline: 65% PFS NeoVira RCC; 75% ADC approval prob. Gross margins 83%; R&D 23%; tax 18%.

Risks: Regulatory (55% Phase II success, $1.5B EBITDA hit on miss); pricing (IRA 9% compress, EU 15% bear); competition (25% immuno erosion); supply (15% inflation); macro (3.5% inflation). $4.5B cash hedges.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Emily Vargas, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Emily Vargas, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. NovaLink's Phase 3 frontline metastatic breast cancer trial is fully enrolled, with topline data expected Q4 2024 that could support BLA submission in H1 2025. RheumaBlock's label expansion into frontline RA is advancing, with Phase 3 interim safety data confirming no new signals. In our gene therapy pipeline, Nova-GT-102 dosing is complete in DMD, showing durable microdystrophin expression. Upcoming milestones include PDUFA for NovaTarg in NSCLC February 2025 and obesity Phase 2b topline Q2 2025. We're on track across six late-stage programs.

Now, I'll hand the call back to David.

David Kwon, CEO:
Thank you, Emily. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, instructions for queuing. Our first question comes from Tim Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Tim Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and good morning. David, on the new launches, NovaLink's share gains against Enhertu and Kadcyla are impressive—can you talk about sustainability into 2025, especially with payer dynamics and competition ramping?

David Kwon, CEO:
Thanks, Tim. Absolutely, the share gains are durable, driven by superior DAR and PFS data, plus 82% compliance via NovaAssist. Payers are aligning at 85% gross-to-net, and Q4 frontline data should expand the pool 20%. We're guiding $1.4-1.6B U.S. peak, with production at 50k vials/month.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, JPMorgan:
Sarah, the EM growth is standout at 35%—what are the biggest risks there, like FX or IP, and how does it factor into 2025 guidance?

Sarah Chen, CFO:
Great question, Lisa. EM at 11% total now, guiding 12% FY with 30%+ growth. Risks like FX are hedged 80%, IP via strong filings. China NRDL volumes 3x U.S., LatAm tenders scaling. Feeds 35% ex-U.S. growth in 2025 guidance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel, Morgan Stanley:
Emily, on catalysts—timing for NovaLink-301 readout and probability? Any updates on obesity?

Dr. Emily Vargas, Chief Medical Officer:
Thanks, Mike. NovaLink-301 topline Q4 2024, HR 0.62 PFS interim; 75% approval prob per models. NovaSlim-OR Q2 2025, 18% weight loss, GI-tolerant vs. injectables. High confidence.

Operator:
Our next question from Rachel Kim with Bank of America.

Rachel Kim, Bank of America:
Sarah, R&D at 28%—priorities shifting? Risks from IRA on assumptions?

Sarah Chen, CFO:
R&D focused oncology 45%, rare 30%; PTRS 25%. Assumptions bake IRA 92% pricing; bear 15% EU erosion. Cash $4.5B covers.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the question-and-answer session.

David Kwon, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the AstraNova Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
